cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T3 answers T2's pull-back directly; T6 takes up T5's silence test.
cells.limitation: T7 urges expressing needs without engaging T6's advice to stop initiating.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T4 adds the friend's possible lack of capacity; T9 uses it: if they cannot meet you.
cells.limitation: T1's utility versus character distinction is never used again.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: T2 versus T3 sets withdrawal against honest disclosure.
cells.limitation: Nobody asks why the friend never initiates; silence-as-test premise in T2 goes unexamined.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T6 recasts Strategist's withdrawal as self-respect rather than power.
cells.limitation: T8 and T9 converge without reconciling T6; section D asserts a consensus.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T9 lands on speaking up as an invitation, with the response as information.
cells.limitation: The open question of the friend's reasons is no sharper at the end than at T1.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T3 names Strategist's pull-back as a control game, a fair reading of T2.
cells.limitation: T6 credits the Strategist with calling chasing draining; T2 and T5 never said that.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T4 questions whether the friend has capacity for the desired friendship.
cells.limitation: T2's assumption that not initiating means not valuing is never challenged or tested.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T1 utility versus character friendship is a recognisable Aristotelian distinction.
cells.limitation: Section D claims consensus the pattern is unsustainable; no turn says so.

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T4 frames the friend's capacity as a question rather than a fact.
cells.limitation: T2, T3, T7 state guesses as facts: time is cheap, silent resentment, only path.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T6 openly announces a changed position and names the Strategist as cause.
cells.limitation: T8 and T9 shift back toward speaking up with no acknowledgment or cause.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern
cells.example: Section A names fear that silence would end the friendship.
cells.limitation: Never separates wanting reciprocity from wanting reassurance; what to say stays undefined.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T2 and T6 build on the user always initiating.
cells.limitation: The user's 'lovely when we meet' detail never shapes any argument.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: Section E branches on how much the user values the friendship.
cells.limitation: Speakers impose dignity and self-respect (T6, T8) as the user's priorities.

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T9 names possibly moving on as the stake of speaking up.
cells.limitation: T3 invents resentment; section D invents unsustainability; friend's circumstances ignored.

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: T8 branches on whether the friend responds with effort.
cells.limitation: No question on duration, whether friend always accepts, or friend's own reasons.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T6 offers self-respect as what drives the wish to stop chasing.
cells.limitation: One motive asserted, no alternatives, no question the user could answer.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T4 surfaces the assumption that the friend can offer the friendship desired.
cells.limitation: Assumption that initiating imbalance signals low regard stays invisible throughout.

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section E sets valuing the friendship against risking an awkward conversation.
cells.limitation: The user's own ranking of closeness versus self-protection is never asked.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: Section A names fear that silence ends the connection.
cells.limitation: Fear of rejection on speaking up is never explored; T3 asserts resentment.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: Section E leaves two branches the user can choose between.
cells.limitation: Section D declares the user's pattern unsustainable instead of offering it for reflection.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options
cells.example: T2, T3, T5 define pull back, speak openly, or state a boundary.
cells.limitation: Accepting the dynamic, named in section A, is dropped after it.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs
cells.example: Section E names the awkward conversation as the cost of speaking up.
cells.limitation: Risk that silence lets a valued friendship fade is never stated as a cost.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: T8: effort in response restores balance; no effort gives an answer.
cells.limitation: Section E conditions on feelings, not on anything the user could observe or count.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T4 names the friend's capacity as the key unknown.
cells.limitation: Friend's reasons and circumstances never separated as the consequential unknown.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps
cells.example: T9 suggests speaking up as an invitation to a more balanced dynamic.
cells.limitation: No concrete wording or small step such as asking the friend to plan next.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T2 is plain: constantly initiating signals your time is cheap.
cells.limitation: T1 and T7 lean on abstractions like common life and virtuous life.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T6 names the Strategist explicitly when conceding.
cells.limitation: T4 agrees silence is not a virtue, a claim no earlier turn made.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Nine turns, all within range, each one short claim.
cells.limitation: Turn lengths are near-uniform, so no turn has room to develop.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices
cells.example: T2 power language distinct from T3 vulnerability language.
cells.limitation: T8 and T9 change positions without saying so; T9 sounds like T8.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Little repetition across nine compact turns.
cells.limitation: T5 repeats T2's silence test without adding to it.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension
cells.example: T2 versus T3: test the friend or confide in them.
cells.limitation: The friendship's possible loss is only touched in T9; tension stays abstract.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals
cells.example: T6 announces a changed mind and names the Strategist.
cells.limitation: T6 cites a claim never made; T8 and T9 reversals have no stated cause.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice
cells.example: T5 Strategist: Silence is the ultimate test.
cells.limitation: Vulnerability Advocate's voice turns generic after T6.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T2 vacuum image: stopping forces the other person to act.
cells.limitation: No analogy or example drawn from the user's lovely meetings.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement
cells.example: T6 reversal briefly shifts momentum.
cells.limitation: Even rhythm and a flat T9 ending; no build or release.

strengths: T4 raises the friend's possible lack of capacity, which T9 turns into a usable exit condition.
T6 makes an explicit, named change of position reframing withdrawal as self-respect.
Section E gives two clear branches: speak up and invite, or pull back and observe.
weaknesses: No mind asks why the friend never initiates or uses the user's 'lovely when we meet' detail.
T8 Strategist and T9 Advocate shift to speaking up with no stated cause; section D invents a consensus.
Minds state guesses as facts (T2 time is cheap, T3 silent resentment) and pose no factual questions.

symptoms.observed: No question about duration, friend's acceptance rate, or friend's reasons; branches rest on feelings.
symptoms.evidence: If they respond with effort, the balance is restored.

symptoms.observed: Premise that not initiating means not valuing is never challenged by any mind.
symptoms.evidence: revealing if they truly value your presence

symptoms.observed: Strategist and Advocate reverse toward speaking up without naming what changed their minds.
symptoms.evidence: So, speak up not to demand, but to invite them

symptoms.observed: Guesses about the user's state and the friend's meaning stated as fact.
symptoms.evidence: intimacy cannot grow in a climate of silent resentment

symptoms.observed: User's 'lovely when we meet' never informs which kind of friendship this is.
symptoms.evidence: is this a friendship of utility or one of character

findings.description: Claims consensus the user's pattern is unsustainable; no turn says this and T6 and T7 diverge.
Credits the Strategist with saying chasing is draining; T2 and T5 argued signalling and power, not drain.
Paraphrased positions attributed to Greene and Brown are plausible but unchecked; no quotations used.

rubric_fit_notes: Matrix fits this relationship decision; the debate's brevity limits evidence across criteria 1 and 4 alike.
question_type_note: Read as a decision about whether to raise the imbalance, so every cell was read as written.
